narrative.overview: This interface is a shared instrument placed beside a live card game. It must read instantly from more than one seat, accept a result in one touch, and disappear from attention between rounds. The existing visual identity is preserved; refinement means stronger spatial behavior, larger reachable controls, clearer focus, and less nonessential UI—not a new theme.
keyCharacteristics: Symmetric, seat-reachable red and blue controls
Dark neutral surfaces with color reserved for team identity and state
Large native buttons with explicit labels
Responsive structure driven by available space, not device names

rules.name: The One-Touch Rule
rules.body: A round result commits immediately. Never add a second confirmation step, Toast, modal, or transient success message.

rules.name: The Shared-Table Rule
rules.body: Duplicate an action entry point only when it materially shortens reach from opposite seats; duplicated undo buttons always operate on the same global history.

rules.name: The Two-Team Rule
rules.body: Red and blue identify sides; every actionable or selected state also needs text, shape, icon, or semantic state. Color alone is forbidden.

rules.name: The Rare Gold Rule
rules.body: Gold appears only for victory. If it appears during ordinary scoring, remove it.

rules.name: The Numeric Anchor Rule
rules.body: The current level is always the largest text. No other number competes with it.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: Resting surfaces use tone or a subtle border. Shadows appear only to communicate state or physical press feedback.

dos: Do preserve the current near-black, red, cyan, white, and victory-gold identity.
Do keep every scoring target at least 44×44 CSS px and aim for 56px height on phones.
Do preserve full keyboard operation with native buttons, visible focus, Enter, and Space.
Do keep the desktop/tablet three-part composition and use the portrait two-column composition.
Do remove spacing and decoration before shrinking labels or touch targets.
Do respect reduced motion, forced colors, zoom, and text enlargement.
donts: Don't build a complex dashboard or add decorative information.
Don't use excessive glow, glassmorphism, or continuous animation that affects recognition.
Don't add confirmation buttons, Toasts, temporary success copy, or modal feedback after scoring.
Don't add the ImageGen concept's 贡牌关系 title, textual relationship bar, or explanatory area; preserve the existing left/right arrow light.
Don't rely on red and blue alone to communicate state.
Don't force portrait-phone users to rotate the device.
Don't use 80vh or unbounded viewport sizing inside a component that shares space with controls and the footer.
